q: How do I calculate the energy and emissions of kiln drying timber per cubic metre?
title: Timber kiln drying: CO2 per cubic metre
short: Log the heat source and the fans. Steam or hot air from a wood waste boiler gives biogenic CO2, shown separately; fossil boilers and electric dehumidifier kilns count fully. Divide the period's fuel and electricity by cubic metres dried, and note species and moisture change, since hardwoods take longer.
audience: Sawmills and furniture makers drying rubberwood, acacia, teak and pine in Vietnam, India and Indonesia

ul: Boiler fuel: wood waste, coal or gas, by kiln if metered.
Electricity for fans and dehumidifiers at the local grid factor.
Hours per charge and cubic metres per charge.

p: Divide by cubic metres dried, and give the starting and final moisture. Drying from green to 8 percent uses far more energy than from air dried.
Kiln drying is often the largest energy step in solid wood furniture, so a measured figure makes a buyer's product footprint far more credible.
